# Getting started with Kimi: a beginner's guide

> **In short:** Kimi is an AI assistant from Moonshot AI that you can use in a web browser at kimi.com. You type a question, it writes an answer. Free access and limits can change, so check kimi.com for current plan details before you rely on it.

Kimi is an AI assistant, which means a program you chat with by typing, the way you would message a helpful friend who knows a lot about many topics. By the end of this guide you will have opened Kimi in your browser, asked your first question, and learned how to ask follow-up questions to get a more useful answer. This guide is written for complete beginners, so you do not need any tech background.

## Before you start
- **A web browser** on a computer, tablet or phone, such as Chrome, Safari, Edge or Firefox.
- **An internet connection.** Kimi runs online, so it will not work offline.
- **An email address** is helpful in case you decide to create an account. You may be able to start without one, depending on what the site offers.
- **Time:** about 10 minutes for the whole guide.

## Step 1 — Open Kimi in your browser
Click the address bar at the top of your browser, type **kimi.com**, and press Enter. The home page should load with a simple chat screen. Look for a large text box near the middle or bottom of the page, often with placeholder words like "Ask anything" or a similar invitation. You may also see a row of suggestions or a menu.

If the page looks different, that is normal, because websites change their layouts often. If you land on a page that is not Kimi, check the spelling of the address and try again. You can also search for "Kimi Moonshot AI" and open the official result.

You'll know it worked when you can see a text box where you can type a message.

## Step 2 — Sign in, or look for a way to start
Some AI assistants let you chat right away, while others ask you to sign in first. Look for a button labeled **Sign in**, **Log in** or **Sign up**, usually in a corner of the screen. If you create an account, you will typically enter an email address and follow the instructions sent to it. Keep your password somewhere safe.

If you do not see a sign-in button and the chat box is already there, you can probably start without an account. Either way, Kimi may show usage limits on free access, so if a message says you have reached a limit, that is the tool telling you something useful, not an error on your part. Plan details can change, so check kimi.com for the current options.

You'll know it worked when you either see your chat screen ready to use or a confirmation that your account is set up.

## Step 3 — Type your first question
Click inside the text box. Type a plain question in ordinary words, the same way you would ask a knowledgeable person. There is no special command to learn. Short, specific questions usually get the best first results.

Next to or below the text box, look for a send button, which is often a small arrow or paper-plane icon. You can also press Enter on your keyboard. Your question appears in the chat, and the answer starts to appear below it, often word by word.

💬 Example: "Explain what a context window is in simple words, using a kitchen example."

If nothing happens after you send, wait a few seconds, since answers can take a moment. If the page shows an error, refresh it and try again. You can also shorten your message.

You'll know it worked when your question appears in the chat and an answer begins to appear underneath it.

## Step 4 — Read the answer and check it
Read the full reply before deciding whether it helps. A good answer usually addresses your question directly and explains its terms. If the reply is too long or too technical, you can say so in the next message.

AI assistants can sound confident even when they are wrong, so check anything important, such as dates, numbers, names, or health and money matters, against a trusted source. Kimi can help you draft, explain and brainstorm, but it can't guarantee every fact. Treat it like a smart first draft, not a final authority.

💬 Example: "Summarize that answer in three short bullet points I could read in under a minute."

If the answer misses the point, do not give up. Rephrase your question with more detail in the next step.

You'll know it worked when you can see a reply you can read and act on, even if you want to adjust it.

## Step 5 — Ask a follow-up question to improve the answer
Type a new message in the same text box, in the same chat. Because the assistant can see the earlier messages in this conversation, you can say things like "make it shorter," "explain it for a teenager," or "give me another example." Each follow-up builds on what came before.

Start a fresh chat if the conversation becomes confusing or you change topics completely. Look for a button or icon labeled **New chat** or a plus sign, usually near the top or on the side. If you do not see it, look for a menu with three lines or three dots in a corner.

💬 Example: "Thanks. Now give me the same explanation again, but for a 10-year-old and in under 80 words."

If the follow-up response goes off track, you can say "Please try again and focus only on [your main topic]." Being specific is the fastest fix.

You'll know it worked when the new answer reflects your change, such as a shorter length or a different level of detail.

## Step 6 — Try a useful everyday prompt
Now try a question from your real life. Kimi works well for tasks like drafting an email, planning a meal, comparing ideas, or explaining a confusing document you paste in. The more context you give, the better the result. Remember to remove private details, such as full addresses, account numbers, or passwords, before you share text with any AI tool.

💬 Example: "Help me write a short, polite email to my landlord asking when the [repair type] will be fixed, and keep it under 100 words."

Read the draft, change any details that are not quite right, and make the final decisions yourself. Kimi can write the words, but it can't send the email for you, and it does not know your situation unless you tell it.

You'll know it worked when you have a draft you can read, edit and use in your own words.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking vague questions and expecting perfect answers.** Fix this by adding detail, such as who the answer is for and how long it should be.
- **Trusting every fact without checking.** Fix this by verifying important numbers, dates and advice with a reliable source.
- **Sharing private information.** Fix this by replacing names, addresses and account numbers with general descriptions before you paste anything.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Kimi can help you plan a trip, explain a recipe substitution, or turn a messy list of errands into a simple schedule.
- **For your business or work:** Kimi can help you draft a meeting agenda, summarize a long document you have the right to share, or brainstorm a list of options for a presentation.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with low-stakes questions, such as asking for a simple recipe or a plain-English explanation of a topic you already know, so you can see how the assistant responds.

## Try it now
Open kimi.com in your browser, type this into the text box, and press send: "Give me three simple ways to use an AI assistant at home this week, each in one sentence."
